newsitem.title: USA: US corporate debt mart quiet in pre-holiday lull.
newsitem.headline: US corporate debt mart quiet in pre-holiday lull.

text.p: An eerie silence has come over the U.S. corporate bond primary market on Monday as players get set to trade in their desks for a day off.
"It's extremely quiet...everyone's just focused on the holiday," said one syndicate source.
The U.S. credit and financial markets will be closed on Wednesday in observance of the Christmas Day holiday.
Corporate debt players will head out early on Tuesday due to an abbreviated trading session, 1400 EST/1900 GMT, before the holiday.
Dealers said despite the slowdown in activity now the new year should see a very active new issue calendar as interest rates remain at their best levels since the spring.
"The calendar is definitely going to pick up...we've heard a number of names already," said one syndicate source.
Meanwhile, among deals expected in the new calendar year are Italy's $1.0 billion 10-year global issue, and State Development Bank of China's $300 million 10-year yankee debt offering, dealers said.
A number of zero coupon bonds are rumored to come to market in the new year as well, dealers said.
Among the issuers expected to tap the market are a number of telecommunications firms, dealers added.

Optelcom is expected to issue $150 million in notes, General Wirless is expected to set $220 million in notes and UIH Australia/Pacific Inc is also expected to set $150 million in notes, dealers added.
Meanwhile, with another holiday on the horizon dealers expect acitivity to remain in a lull as the calendar year comes to a close.
Next Wednesday, the credit and financial markets will close for the New Year's Day holiday.
Currently, the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond is up 14/32 at 99-2/32 to yield 6.57 percent.
